title: Ep184 深圳生存手册：大量新鲜的搞钱方式涌入我的脑子
title_en: Ep184 Shenzhen Survival Manual: A Flood of Fresh Ways to Make Money Rushed Into My Head
eyebrow: City Life & Society · 城市生活与社会
summary_cn: 毛冬携宁嘉宇、小块、大雄、风哥及现场观众，在《基本无害》深圳站现场录制城市生存手册：拆解「全员搞钱」刻板印象，从城中村握手楼、莲花山塑料浴、领军人才落户到华强北美妆出海，呈现一座移民城市如何在房价压力下仍让人相信「还有机会」
summary_en: Host Mao Dong brings Ning Jiayu, Xiao Kuai, Da Xiong, Feng Ge, and a live audience together for a Shenzhen edition of the podcast Basically Harmless. Together they bust the stereotype that "everyone in Shenzhen is just chasing money," walking through the city's real texture: the handshake buildings of urban villages, plastic-bag baths at Lotus Hill bathhouses, the "leading talent" residency program, and Huaqiangbei beauty brands going overseas. The portrait that emerges is of a migrant city where, despite crushing housing prices, people still believe there's a chance.

scenes.title_cn: 一、城市身份与人口结构
scenes.context: 讨论深圳「没有土著」的身份分层：村里人、深三代、领军人才、打工人。语域：casual 现场脱口秀 + 城市观察。
scenes.speak: Shenzhen has almost no "native" narrative — identity is layered by when you moved in and what the residency policy says: pre-special-zone villagers, third-generation builders' descendants, tax-paying leading talents, and ordinary workers. The key insight: "Once you arrive, you're a Shenzhener" is a policy slogan — your actual experience depends on your hukou, your property, and your industry. The typical situation: deciding whether to apply for residency, choosing between an urban village or the far suburbs for rent, and whether starting a business here is worth betting on Shenzhen's policies. Feng Ge calls himself a "leading talent who got paid to become a Shenzhener": a company paying several million in tax can earn an official title plus yearly subsidies. Da Xiong came from Chaoshan with his parents at age three, so he considers himself a local — just not a native. It's the opposite of Beijing and Shanghai, where "failing to get residency turns you artsy" — Shenzhen's residency still feels reachable, so people are willing to grind harder. Mao Dong himself came in 2014 because a partner was starting a business here; had he gone to Beijing, he says he might have been just "a directionless artsy youth." Back then Shenzhen was cheaper to start a business in than Shanghai and had fewer artsy kids than Beijing — "only Shenzhen had this power to force talent into action." Everything turned smooth once they moved from a remote Longhua-Buji office to the Science and Technology Park.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：深圳几乎没有「纯土著」叙事，身份按迁入时间与户籍政策分层：特区前村里人、深三代建设者后代、纳税领军人才、普通打工人
sentences.en: Shenzhen has almost no "pure native" narrative — identity is layered by when you moved in and what the hukou policy says: pre-special-zone villagers, third-generation builder descendants, tax-paying leading talents, and ordinary workers.
sentences.note: 表达提示native → 土著；hukou / residency policy → 户籍政策；leading talent → 领军人才；migrant worker → 打工人

sentences.cn: 关键理解：「来了就是深圳人」是政策口号，实际体验取决于户口、房产与行业
sentences.en: The key insight: "Once you arrive, you're a Shenzhener" is a policy slogan — your real experience depends on your hukou, your property, and your industry.
sentences.note: 表达提示policy slogan → 政策口号；depend on → 取决于；property → 房产

sentences.cn: 典型场景：评估自己是否要落户、租房选城中村还是远郊、创业是否值得押注深圳政策
sentences.en: The typical situation: weighing whether to apply for residency, choosing between an urban village or the far suburbs for rent, and whether starting a business here is worth betting on Shenzhen's policies.
sentences.note: 表达提示apply for residency → 落户；urban village → 城中村；bet on → 押注；far suburbs → 远郊

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：风哥自称「收了钱当深圳人」的领军人才，公司纳税达几百万可获官方 title 及每年补贴；大雄三岁随父母从潮汕来，自认本地但非土著
sentences.en: Feng Ge calls himself a "leading talent who got paid to become a Shenzhener": a company paying several million in tax can earn an official title plus yearly subsidies. Da Xiong came from Chaoshan with his parents at age three, so he considers himself a local — just not a native.
sentences.note: 表达提示official title → 官方头衔；subsidy → 补贴；considers himself a local → 自认本地人

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：与北上「落不了户反而更文艺」形成对照，深圳因落户仍有希望而让人更愿意拼搏
sentences.en: It contrasts with Beijing and Shanghai, where "failing to get residency turns you more artsy." In Shenzhen, because residency still feels achievable, people are more willing to hustle.
sentences.note: 表达提示contrast with → 与…形成对照；artsy → 文艺的；achievable → 仍有希望；hustle → 拼搏

sentences.cn: 2014年因合伙人在深圳创业而来，若去北京可能只是「无所事事的文艺青年」。深圳当时创业环境比上海便宜，比北京少文艺青年——「只有深圳才有这种逼学力人才」。从龙华布吉偏远办公室搬到科技园后，一切变顺利
sentences.en: He came in 2014 because a partner was starting a business in Shenzhen; had he gone to Beijing, he might have been just "a directionless artsy youth." Back then Shenzhen was cheaper for startups than Shanghai and had fewer artsy kids than Beijing — "only Shenzhen had this power to push talent into action." Everything turned smooth once they moved from a remote Longhua-Buji office to the Science and Technology Park.
sentences.note: 表达提示directionless → 无所事事的；startup → 创业；push talent into action → 逼人才行动；Science and Technology Park → 科技园

paraphrase.intent: 想说「深圳没有原住民文化」
phrases: There's no native identity to speak of here.
Everyone's a migrant — that's the whole point.
paraphrase.chunks: no native identity · everyone's a migrant
paraphrase.usage: 第一句客观陈述，第二句更有脱口秀味道

paraphrase.intent: 想说「落户政策是吸引力来源」
phrases: The residency path is what keeps people grinding.
A reachable hukou makes all the difference.
paraphrase.chunks: keep people grinding · a reachable hukou · make all the difference
paraphrase.usage: grind 是「苦干」的口语词；make all the difference 强调决定性作用

phrases: Shenzhen pushes you to get your act together.
The city's vibe practically forces you to hustle.
paraphrase.chunks: push you · get your act together · forces you to hustle
paraphrase.usage: get your act together 口语有力；force to hustle 偏点评

scenes.context: 城中村握手楼与深圳水汇的独特体验。语域：casual 现场分享 + 生活方式观察。
scenes.speak: Shenzhen's urban villages are high-density buildings of four to seven-plus stories built by locals — they look like normal apartment blocks from outside, but the density is extreme; rare in Nanshan, everywhere elsewhere. The practical tip: check the building type before renting; enjoy the cheap, smoky life of first-floor food stalls and malatang, but accept the crowding and lack of privacy. Severity: moderate — it affects the living experience, not life itself. As the guests put it, they're "handshake buildings" where "you can open your window and practically shake hands with your neighbor." Northern friends often can't even recognize an urban village and mistake it for normal housing. On the social side, newcomers get taken to climb Lianhua Mountain. The bathhouses have their own rules: disposable plastic underwear, bathing in plastic bags, and a deeply rooted tipping culture, from a minimum of ten yuan up to a hundred. The honest take: overall, northern bathhouse experiences beat Shenzhen's — few free meals, and the tipping culture runs deep.

sentences.cn: 原因：深圳城中村是本地人自建四五层至七八层高密度楼，外观像小区但密度极高，南山较少、其他区遍地
sentences.en: The cause: Shenzhen's urban villages are high-density buildings of four to seven-plus stories, self-built by locals. They look like regular apartment complexes but pack extreme density — rare in Nanshan, everywhere in other districts.
sentences.note: 表达提示high-density building → 高密度楼；apartment complex → 小区；self-built → 自建

sentences.cn: 解法：租房前确认楼栋类型；利用一层大排档、麻辣烫的烟火气低成本生活，但需接受拥挤与隐私缺失
sentences.en: The fix: check the building type before renting; live cheaply off the bustle of first-floor food stalls and malatang, but accept the crowding and the lack of privacy.
sentences.note: 表达提示food stall / daipaidang → 大排档；malatang → 麻辣烫；lack of privacy → 隐私缺失

sentences.cn: 严重程度：小心（影响居住体验，非致命）
sentences.en: Severity: moderate — it affects the living experience, not life itself.
sentences.note: 表达提示living experience → 居住体验；not life itself → 非致命

sentences.cn: （引用）嘉宾说法：「你打开窗户就可以伸手握到对方」的握手楼；北方朋友常认不出城中村，误以为是正常住宅
sentences.en: The guests call them "handshake buildings": "open your window and you can reach out and shake your neighbor's hand." Northern friends often fail to recognize an urban village and mistake it for ordinary housing.
sentences.note: 表达提示handshake building → 握手楼；mistake A for B → 误以为 A 是 B

sentences.cn: 核心机制：来深圳常被带去爬莲花山；水汇（洗浴中心）有独特规矩：一次性塑料内裤、穿着塑料袋泡澡，且普遍收小费（最低十元，有的高达一百）
sentences.en: The mechanism: newcomers to Shenzhen often get taken to climb Lianhua Mountain. Bathhouses have their own rules: disposable plastic underwear, bathing in plastic bags, and a widespread tipping culture — a minimum of 10 yuan, sometimes up to 100.
sentences.note: 表达提示bathhouse / shuihui → 水汇/洗浴中心；disposable underwear → 一次性内裤；tipping culture → 小费文化

sentences.cn: 关键理解：北方整体洗浴体验优于深圳——深圳水汇少有免费餐食，小费文化根深蒂固
sentences.en: The key insight: northern bathhouses generally offer a better experience than Shenzhen's — few free meals, and the tipping culture runs deep.
sentences.note: 表达提示runs deep → 根深蒂固；free meal → 免费餐食；generally better → 整体更优

paraphrase.intent: 想说「城中村看着像小区其实挤爆了」
phrases: They look like normal housing but pack people like sardines.
From outside it's a regular block; inside it's a vertical crowd.
paraphrase.chunks: pack people like sardines · a vertical crowd
paraphrase.usage: sardines 比喻很口语形象；vertical crowd 是书面新词

paraphrase.intent: 想说「住城中村便宜但有代价」
phrases: Cheap rent comes with a privacy tax.
You trade comfort for affordability.
paraphrase.chunks: a privacy tax · trade A for B
paraphrase.usage: a privacy tax 是俏皮说法；trade A for B 是通用结构

paraphrase.intent: 想说「南方浴场不如北方」
phrases: Northern bathhouses blow Shenzhen's out of the water.
When it comes to bathhouses, the north just does it better.
paraphrase.chunks: blow out of the water · when it comes to
paraphrase.usage: blow out of the water 夸张口语；when it comes to 引出话题

scenes.title_cn: 三、社交、文艺与城市气质
scenes.context: 房价与分散居住如何压缩社交、深圳的文艺土壤，以及港式茶餐厅「走」字菜单的趣事。语域：casual 现场闲聊 + 文化观察。
scenes.speak: Housing prices rank among China's highest, so people live far apart — Bao'an to Nanshan is dozens of kilometers — making meetups expensive; add the work-and-money culture, and socializing gives way to individual hustle. The key insight: it's not that nobody cares about you; it's physical distance plus scarce time. Unlike Beijing and Shanghai, where people who can't get residency "goof off happily," Shenzheners feel there's still a chance and don't want to waste it. As one guest says, "I've lost touch with so many old friends." Shenzhen hosted the first hip-hop awards ceremony in Futian for years, but signed no artists and missed the explosion. Compared with the north: Beijing has the charm of not getting residency, full of artsy kids; Shenzhen has produced almost no star singers, and seven years of promoting hip-hop culture barely made money. On everyday culture: Hong Kong-style cafe menus follow Hong Kong habits, where "zou bing" means no ice and "zou qingcai" means no vegetables. Outsiders misread "zou" as "add one," and ordering "no veg, no beef balls, no pork balls" just brings a bowl of plain noodles. So confirm before ordering: "zou" means remove, not add.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：房价中国第一档，大家住得分散（宝安到南山几十公里），聚会成本高；加上加班搞钱文化，社交让位于个人奋斗
sentences.en: The mechanism: housing prices are in China's top tier, so people live far apart — Bao'an to Nanshan is dozens of kilometers — making gatherings expensive. Add the overtime-and-money culture, and socializing gives way to individual hustle.
sentences.note: 表达提示top tier → 第一档；give way to → 让位于；individual hustle → 个人奋斗

sentences.cn: 关键理解：不是没人理你，是物理距离+时间稀缺；与北京上海「落不了户反而天天傻乐」不同，深圳人觉得还有机会、不想虚度
sentences.en: The key insight: it's not that nobody cares — it's physical distance plus scarce time. Unlike Beijing and Shanghai, where people "goof off happily" without residency, Shenzheners feel there's still a chance and don't want to waste it.
sentences.note: 表达提示scarce time → 时间稀缺；goof off → 傻乐/虚度；waste it → 虚度光阴

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「好多以前的朋友都断了」；深圳第一个嘻哈颁奖典礼在福田办了很多年，但没签约艺人错过爆火红利
sentences.en: "I've lost touch with so many old friends." Shenzhen hosted the first hip-hop awards ceremony in Futian for years, but signed no artists and missed the boom.
sentences.note: 表达提示lose touch with → 和…断了联系；awards ceremony → 颁奖典礼；miss the boom → 错过爆火红利

sentences.cn: （引用）与北上对比：北京有落不上户的魅力，文艺青年多；深圳没出几个明星歌手，嘻哈文化推广七年几乎不赚钱
sentences.en: Compared with the north: Beijing has the charm of unreachable residency and plenty of artsy youth; Shenzhen has produced almost no star singers, and seven years of promoting hip-hop culture barely turned a profit.
sentences.note: 表达提示artsy youth → 文艺青年；turn a profit → 赚钱；unreachable → 落不上户的

sentences.cn: 核心机制：港式茶餐厅菜单沿香港习惯，「走冰」=去冰，「走青菜」=不要青菜。外地人误把「走」理解成「来一个」，点「走青菜走牛肉丸走猪肉丸」结果上了一碗素面
sentences.en: The mechanism: Hong Kong-style cha chaan teng menus follow Hong Kong habits — "zou bing" means no ice, "zou qingcai" means no vegetables. Outsiders misread "zou" as "add one," so ordering "zou qingcai, zou niurouwan, zou zhurouwan" just brings a bowl of plain noodles.
sentences.note: 表达提示cha chaan teng → 港式茶餐厅；misread → 误读；plain noodles → 素面

sentences.cn: 怎么用：点餐前确认「走」=去掉/不要，而非添加
sentences.en: How to use it: before ordering, confirm that "zou" means remove or skip — not add.
sentences.note: 表达提示remove / skip → 去掉；add → 添加；before ordering → 点餐前

paraphrase.intent: 想说「大家住得太远聚会太贵」
phrases: Getting together is a cross-city commute.
A dinner meetup is practically a day trip here.
paraphrase.usage: cross-city commute 描述距离成本；day trip 夸张但形象

paraphrase.intent: 想说「不是冷漠，是没时间」
phrases: It's not unfriendliness — it's scheduling math.
People aren't cold; they just have no bandwidth.
paraphrase.usage: no bandwidth 是口语化「没精力」的职场词

paraphrase.intent: 想说「菜单里的字和你理解的不一样」
phrases: The menu word means the opposite of what you'd guess.
A single character can flip your whole order.
paraphrase.chunks: the opposite of what you'd guess · flip your order
paraphrase.usage: flip 表示「整个反转」，幽默又准确

scenes.title_cn: 四、搞钱生态：政策、创业与副业
scenes.title_en: 4. The Money-Making Ecosystem: Policy, Startups & Side Hustles
scenes.context: 深圳的免费公益课、创业补贴、税收优惠，以及大雄副业开餐厅的真实账本。语域：casual 现场访谈 + 政策实操。
scenes.speak: Each district's "Wenti Tong" app offers free or cheap community classes in adult calligraphy, vocal music, and tennis. College-student startups get office subsidies and monthly grants, and Shenzhen's tax incentives attract people from other cities just to register companies here. The boundary: rich cultural subsidies don't mean the arts industry is mature; subsidies come with eligibility and expiration, so you have to keep watching policy updates. As the guests share: one got six free tennis lessons; Mahua FunAge tickets were half price on Nanshan's Wenti Tong; a former Beijing resident came to Shenzhen specifically to register a company and save on tax. To apply it: download your district's Wenti Tong app and sign up for free classes; apply for startup subsidies if eligible; and compare registration tax rates before picking your company's location. Da Xiong runs two western restaurants in Nanshan — the Westwood Qianhai location, plus a Hong Kong branch — ranked number one on the ambiance list. When Xiao Kuai pressed him on whether it's "a hobby or actually profitable," he admitted: profitable. Time can be squeezed out — and as he says, "you can squeeze out money too." As the quote goes, "Xiao Kuai thought there were only two options for starting a business: either out of passion, or for money. You never thought there could be a third option."

sentences.cn: 核心机制：各区「文体通」APP 提供成人书法、声乐、网球等免费或低价公益课；大学生创业有办公室补贴和每月资助；深圳公司税收优惠吸引外地人专门来注册
sentences.en: The mechanism: each district's "Wenti Tong" app offers free or cheap community classes in adult calligraphy, vocal music, and tennis. College-student startups get office subsidies and monthly grants, and Shenzhen's tax incentives draw people from other cities specifically to register companies here.
sentences.note: 表达提示community class → 公益课；calligraphy → 书法；vocal music → 声乐；tax incentive → 税收优惠；register a company → 注册公司

sentences.cn: 适用边界：文化补贴丰富不代表文艺产业成熟；补贴有门槛和时效，需持续关注政策更新
sentences.en: The boundary: abundant cultural subsidies don't mean the arts industry is mature; subsidies come with eligibility and expiration, so keep an eye on policy updates.
sentences.note: 表达提示eligibility → 门槛/资格；expiration → 时效；policy update → 政策更新；keep an eye on → 持续关注

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：嘉宾免费学了六节网球；开心麻花票在南山文体通半价；北京前客特意来深圳办公司省税
sentences.en: Evidence: one guest took six free tennis lessons; Mahua FunAge tickets were half price on Nanshan's Wenti Tong; a former Beijing resident came to Shenzhen specifically to register a company and save on tax.
sentences.note: 表达提示half price → 半价；specifically to → 特意为了；save on tax → 省税

sentences.cn: （引用）怎么落地：下载宝安/南山等区文体通报名免费课程；符合条件申请创业补贴；比较注册地税率再决定公司选址
sentences.en: How to apply it: download your district's Wenti Tong app and sign up for free classes; apply for startup subsidies if you qualify; and compare registration tax rates before choosing your company's location.
sentences.note: 表达提示sign up for → 报名；if you qualify → 符合条件；company location → 公司选址

sentences.cn: 在南山开两家西餐厅（Westwood 浅海店），香港也有分店，环境榜排第一。被小块追问「爱好还是真赚钱」后坦白：真赚钱。时间可以挤出来，「钱你也可以挤出来」
sentences.en: He runs two western restaurants in Nanshan — the Westwood Qianhai location, plus a Hong Kong branch — ranked first on the ambiance list. When Xiao Kuai pressed him on whether it's "a hobby or actually profitable," he admitted: it's actually profitable. Time can be squeezed out — and "you can squeeze out money too."
sentences.note: 表达提示ambiance list → 环境榜；press sb on → 追问；profitable → 真赚钱；squeeze out → 挤出来

sentences.cn: （引用）"小块以为创业只有两种选择，要不然是出于爱好，要不然是赚钱。你没有想过能有个同志。"
sentences.en: "Xiao Kuai thought starting a business had only two options: either out of passion, or for money. You never imagined there could be a third way."
sentences.note: 表达提示out of passion → 出于爱好；a third way → 第三种选择

paraphrase.intent: 想说「补贴多但不等于产业成熟」
phrases: Subsidies are generous, but the industry itself is still young.
Free classes don't add up to a mature arts scene.
paraphrase.chunks: subsidies are generous · a mature arts scene
paraphrase.usage: generous 形容补贴多；add up to 表示「凑不成」

paraphrase.intent: 想说「副业做得比主业还赚钱」
phrases: The side hustle outearns the day job.
What started as a side thing became his real money maker.
paraphrase.usage: outearn 简洁有力；money maker 口语

paraphrase.intent: 想说「创业不只有爱好或赚钱两种」
phrases: Passion and profit aren't the only two boxes.
There's a whole spectrum between hobby and hustle.
paraphrase.chunks: the only two boxes · a whole spectrum
paraphrase.usage: boxes 比喻「分类选项」；spectrum 表示光谱/连续区间

scenes.title_cn: 五、反面案例与人生选择
scenes.context: 小块作为「来了深圳没搞到钱」的代表，与林老板的对比，以及深圳高房价下的选择逻辑。语域：casual 现场对谈 + 人生思考。
scenes.speak: Xiao Kuai represents the side of "came to Shenzhen but didn't strike it rich." He cares about others' startup success stories precisely because he's failed himself. The key insight: behind the Shenzhen money myth stands a huge crowd of silent losers — not everyone moves at Boss Lin's speed. The contrast: in the same city, one man earns in two years what it takes others two or three years to lose, while someone else is still fumbling around. Why it matters: under crushing housing prices, losing hope slides into anxiety; Shenzhen's uniqueness is that migrants still choose to work overtime and fight, unlike some in Beijing and Shanghai who settle for "forget it." The boundary: if you're after an artsy atmosphere, tight-knit social circles, or a cheap life of leisure, cities like Beijing and Chengdu might suit you better; if you already have stable remote income, Shenzhen's sky-high housing prices demand a re-calculated cost-benefit. As the line goes, "Maybe everyone who comes to Shenzhen feels: I still have a chance, I want to fight and work overtime… nobody wants to waste their life."

sentences.cn: 核心机制：小块代表「来了深圳但没搞到钱」的一面，关心别人创业成功故事正因为自己失败过
sentences.en: The mechanism: Xiao Kuai represents the "came to Shenzhen but didn't strike it rich" side. He cares about others' startup success stories precisely because he has failed himself.
sentences.note: 表达提示strike it rich → 搞到钱/发财；precisely because → 正因为；success story → 成功故事

sentences.cn: 关键理解：深圳搞钱神话背后有大量沉默失败者；不是所有人都有林老板式的赚钱速度
sentences.en: The key insight: behind the Shenzhen money myth stands a large crowd of silent losers; not everyone moves at Boss Lin's speed.
sentences.note: 表达提示money myth → 搞钱神话；silent losers → 沉默的失败者；at sb's speed → 某人的速度

sentences.cn: （引用）与林老板对比：同样在深圳，有人两年赚够别人两三年赔的，有人仍在摸索
sentences.en: The contrast with Boss Lin: in the same city, one man earns in two years what it takes others two or three to lose, while someone else is still figuring things out.
sentences.note: 表达提示earn in two years what others lose in three → 两年赚别人两三年赔的；figure things out → 摸索

sentences.cn: 为什么重要：房价高压下若失去希望会陷入焦虑；深圳的独特之处在于移民仍愿加班拼搏，而非像北上部分人群选择「算了」
sentences.en: Why it matters: under housing-price pressure, losing hope slides into anxiety. Shenzhen's uniqueness is that migrants still choose to work overtime and fight, unlike some people in Beijing and Shanghai who opt for "forget it."
sentences.note: 表达提示slides into → 陷入；opt for → 选择；forget it → 算了

sentences.cn: 适用边界：若追求文艺氛围、紧密社交或低成本躺平，北京成都等可能更合适；若已有稳定远程收入，深圳高房价性价比需重算
sentences.en: The boundary: if you're after an artsy atmosphere, tight-knit social circles, or cheap and easy living, cities like Beijing and Chengdu may suit you better; if you already earn stable remote income, Shenzhen's high housing prices demand recalculating the value.
sentences.note: 表达提示tight-knit social circle → 紧密社交圈；easy living → 躺平；recalculate → 重算；suit you better → 更适合你

sentences.cn: （引用）"可能大家来深圳都会觉得，我还是有机会的，我想拼一拼多加班……就大家不想虚度。"
sentences.en: "Maybe everyone who comes to Shenzhen feels: I still have a chance, I want to fight and put in the overtime… nobody wants to waste their life."
sentences.note: 表达提示I still have a chance → 我还有机会；put in the overtime → 多加班；waste one's life → 虚度

paraphrase.intent: 想说「光鲜背后有大量没成功的人」
phrases: For every winner, there's a silent crowd who didn't make it.
The success stories hide the ones who quietly missed.
paraphrase.chunks: for every winner · didn't make it · quietly missed
paraphrase.usage: make it 是口语「成功」；quietly missed 文学化

phrases: Nobody here wants to coast — the clock is running.
The vibe is: keep pushing, don't drift.
paraphrase.usage: coast 表示「不费力混着过」；drift 表示「随波逐流」

paraphrase.intent: 想说「不是所有人都适合深圳」
phrases: Shenzhen isn't for everyone — know what you're optimizing for.
If it's art, community, or cheap rest you want, look elsewhere.
paraphrase.chunks: isn't for everyone · optimizing for · look elsewhere
paraphrase.usage: optimizing for 是理性的说法；look elsewhere 口语建议

practice.cn: 用「strike it rich」说：不是所有人来深圳都能发财。
practice.en: Not everyone who moves to Shenzhen strikes it rich.

practice.cn: 用「handshake building」说：城中村握手楼密度极高。
practice.en: The handshake buildings pack you in so tight you can touch your neighbor's window.

practice.cn: 用「press sb on」说：小块追问餐厅到底赚不赚钱。
practice.en: Xiao Kuai pressed him on whether the restaurant actually made money.

practice.cn: 用「coast」说：深圳人不想混日子。
practice.en: People here don't want to coast — they'd rather fight for a chance.

pitfalls.wrong: Shenzhen has no old people who were born there.
pitfalls.right: Shenzhen has almost no "native" narrative — identity is layered by residency policy.
pitfalls.why: 「土著」直译成 people born there 会误导（本地出生的人其实有）；用 native narrative / identity 指身份叙事更准确。

pitfalls.wrong: You can open the window and hold hands with the neighbor.
pitfalls.right: Open your window and you can practically shake hands with your neighbor.
pitfalls.why: 握手楼是比喻「距离近到能握手」，用 practically shake hands 保留修辞，直译 hold hands（牵手）语义错误。

pitfalls.wrong: The bathhouse charges tips from ten yuan to one hundred yuan.
pitfalls.right: Tipping is widespread, from a 10-yuan minimum up to 100.
pitfalls.why: 小费是「接受/惯例」而非「强制收费」，用 tipping is widespread 描述文化现象更自然。

pitfalls.wrong: I don't have time and no money, I want to lie flat.
pitfalls.right: With a stable remote income, the math for Shenzhen's housing changes completely.
pitfalls.why: 躺平直译 lie flat 在英文里指「平躺」；表达「不奋斗的安逸生活」用 easy living / coast / opt out 更贴切。

shifts.before: 以为深圳人人都在搞钱、没有生活
shifts.after: 深圳也有文艺、社区与市井文化，「搞钱」是环境逼出来的选择而非天性

shifts.before: 以为落户口号「来了就是深圳人」人人平等
shifts.after: 实际体验取决于户口、房产与行业，身份是分层而多元的

shifts.before: 以为深圳神话=每个人都能快速暴富
shifts.after: 神话背后有大量沉默失败者；深圳真正特别的是「仍然相信有机会」的移民心态
